criterion_weight_scope: Numeric and semantic criterion weights describe their local diagnostic scores. Final strict settlement is defined by scoring_params.

numeric_criteria.observable: Every required work package exactly once
Full duration inside a permitted continuous window, respecting readiness and tool availability
Correct crews/tools and no shared-resource collision
Replacement finishes before the paired test
Feasible ordered objectives from public planning conditions; accept equivalent starts
Candidate-dependent energization, continuous48h standby,14 calendar day report deadline and one calendar month oil follow-up
Daily marks agree with actual candidate dates

semantic_criteria.description: Preserve the Golden's scope grain: 19 radiator groups are one four-transformer total with no invented per-transformer allocation; S remains one package containing its source-listed auxiliary equipment; and T common-enclosure bus and S dock bus remain separate package scopes. An explicit prose comparison is not required when the workbook structure and scope text preserve the distinction. Score 1 for all three meanings, 0.5 for one material omission without contradiction, and 0 for a false count, allocation, aggregation, or merged area identity.

Treat M readiness as a release assumption rather than proof of arrival, and defer or replan both M and the paired T test when replacement cannot proceed. Score 1 for both controls, 0.5 for one with no contrary claim, and 0 for asserted readiness or an independently proceeding T plan.

State that package durations are planning estimates rather than observed or manufacturer-standard durations and remain subject to pre-start confirmation. Score 1 when both the provisional status and confirmation boundary are present, otherwise 0.

Apply the documented ordered objective: among feasible plans first finish T as early as possible, then among ties finish all site work as early as possible. Score 1 only when the ordering and both objectives are preserved, otherwise 0.

The adopted T milestone must be feasible under the public M/T precedence, continuous-duration, readiness and closure constraints. Accept a correct schedule and consistent milestone without a written lower-bound proof, enumeration or derivation; these extra explanations are optional. Score 1 for a feasible T milestone and 0 for an infeasible or missing milestone. The historical item identifier is retained only for compatibility.

Preserve the public source's two execution boundaries: site work remains conditional on the approved work plan and applicable outage/work permission; package completion includes the source-required restoration, cleanup and handover rather than only the main intervention or test. Accept integrated workbook-wide conditions and equivalent cross-sheet evidence. Do not additionally require a separate blanket statement that every construction activity is subject to general test-readiness confirmation; the source's test and instrument controls apply in their stated operational context. Score 1 when both pre-start approval/permission and closeout meanings are preserved, 0.5 for one complete meaning with no contradiction, and 0 for an explicit materially unsafe approval, permission or completion boundary.

Treat every listed energization time as a candidate milestone requiring passed tests, restoration, handover and operator permission; recognize that circuit-to-protection associations are absent and package completion cannot establish independent energization. Workbook-wide release conditions and package completion definitions apply to all corresponding candidate nodes; do not require the same condition to be repeated in every row. Read cross-sheet evidence together, while respecting any explicit local override. Score 1 for both the release conditions and missing-association boundary, 0.5 for only one, and 0 for treating a planned package finish as authorization or completed energization.

Keep actual completion, test, permission and energization status pending where the inputs provide no result, and require relevant changes to propagate through paired M/T work and the standby, report and oil-analysis dates that depend on actual events. Score 1 for pending-state discipline plus this downstream propagation, 0.5 for one of them, and 0 for fabricated actual completion or explicitly frozen dependent dates.

Define standby as 48 continuous hours from actual energization, including closed site-work days; retain the two-hour response obligation and the public source's separately staffed arrangement that does not consume construction crews. A prospective programme may display standby from candidate energization when its workbook-wide actual-event rule requires the corresponding downstream nodes to be recalculated or shifted; this is equivalent to stating the actual trigger in every standby row. Read these conditions together and do not require automatic formulas. Score 1 for all meanings, 0.5 for an incomplete but noncontradictory arrangement, and 0 for explicit working-day standby, use of undeclared construction capacity, or a fixed planned end that remains unchanged despite delayed actual energization.

Bind the written test report deadline to actual completion of all site work using the source two-week/14-calendar-day rule, while labeling the displayed date provisional. Score 1 for trigger, duration and provisional status, 0.5 for a correct displayed provisional date with an incomplete trigger rule, and 0 for a fixed or incorrectly triggered deadline.

Bind the transformer oil follow-up to actual in-service date plus one calendar month and preserve chromatography, moisture and simplified testing. Score 1 for the trigger, calendar rule and complete test scope, 0.5 for a correct provisional date and trigger with incomplete test scope, and 0 for a 30-day/working-day rule, wrong trigger, or cancellation.

artifact_operational_criteria.description: A workbook-contained, reproducible validation receipt for interval/resource feasibility and the ordered T/site result; equivalent methods count and a written proof is not required.
A formula-driven or structured manual mechanism for recording actual events, rechecking affected feasibility and updating Gantt and follow-up nodes.

accepted variation: Accept any source-supported business-equivalent result; programmatic facts and semantic actions have distinct ownership.
